technical_and_design_decisions: Work is performed on the existing Spring XD codebase implied by the user stories (streams, jobs, hdfs-dataset sink, Mail sink, Rabbit source/sink modules, Boot-based runtime); no greenfield development.

U2: Add a 'codec' option to the hdfs-dataset sink for Avro output. Default remains snappy for backward compatibility; values 'none'/'null' disable compression and any Hadoop CompressionCodec short name (e.g., gzip, bzip2, default) is accepted and resolved via Hadoop's CompressionCodecFactory.

U3: Extend the Mail sink module XML configuration with a 'java-mail-properties' attribute that accepts a reference to a <util:properties/> bean, passed through to the Spring Integration mail adapters exactly as documented for secured IMAPS/SMTPS; existing non-TLS configuration remains unchanged.

U4: Add 'partitionResultsTimeout' to the job module metadata so it is surfaced for every job importing the singlestep-partitioning strategy, and explicitly wire it into the 3 out-of-the-box job definitions; update the wiki metadata tables.

U5: Centralize all ~35 dependency versions in the Gradle build properties and align them with Spring Boot 1.2.0 dependency management; perform the upgrade in one branch with the full regression suite executed before merge.

U6: Support an external YAML deployment manifest (e.g., 'stream deploy --propertiesFile <path>.yml') parsed with SnakeYAML, whose entries are merged with (and take defined precedence over) inline deployment properties in the stream definition.

U7: Implement compression as a message-bus codec abstraction supporting gzip and zip (both compress and decompress), configurable per stream via bus properties, built on Spring Integration's compression transformers where possible.
U8: Expose compression on the Rabbit source and sink modules as module options that reuse the U7 codec implementation (compress on sink, decompress on source), avoiding duplicated logic.

The generic Spring Framework description (including the Spring 6 / Java 17 note) is treated as context only; the actual target platform is the Spring XD stack described in U5 (Spring Boot 1.2.0, Spring 4.1.3) running on the JDK supported by that stack.
assumptions: A single developer (the author) performs all work full-time and is already familiar with the Spring XD codebase and its build system.
Development workstation, source control, and CI infrastructure already exist and require no procurement.
A 3-node Hadoop test cluster with HDFS and Sqoop is available for the U1 benchmark and U2 integration tests; benchmark execution time is counted as attended work.
Secured test mail servers (TLS IMAP/SMTP) are provided via locally hosted test containers (e.g., GreenMail with SSL or equivalent), so no external mail infrastructure is needed.
The Boot 1.2.0 upgrade involves typical minor API breakages only; estimate includes fixing compilation errors and failing regression tests, but no redesign of XD features.
Documentation work consists of module README/metadata and wiki updates; no formal user-guide authoring is required.
Testing effort covers unit and integration tests written by the developer, including the benchmark runs for U1 (the developer also performs the QA benchmarking).
Estimates are effort (workdays), not elapsed duration; context switching between stories is not separately padded.
No clarifying questions were permitted, so ambiguous scope points were resolved with the reasonable interpretations recorded above.

activities.activity_description: Provision/verify the Hadoop test cluster, install and configure Sqoop, prepare the relational source schema and representative test dataset, and define the benchmark data volumes.
Create repeatable benchmark scripts, the Sqoop jobs and the equivalent jdbchdfs batch job definitions, and metrics collection (timings, throughput, resource stats).

activities.activity_name: Execute benchmark runs and collect metrics (U1)
activities.activity_description: Run Sqoop and jdbchdfs jobs across the agreed scenarios, repeat runs for consistency, and record performance statistics.
Analyze collected metrics, compare and contrast Sqoop vs. jdbchdfs performance, and write the findings report.
Add a 'codec' option to the hdfs-dataset sink for Avro files: allow disabling snappy and selecting an alternative Hadoop compression codec, with backward-compatible defaults.
Unit and integration tests covering snappy default, disabled compression, and alternative codecs, verifying written Avro files on HDFS.
Update sink module metadata and wiki documentation describing the new codec option and its values.
Add the 'java-mail-properties' attribute to the Mail sink adapter configuration so a <util:properties/> bean with SSL/TLS properties can be supplied for secured IMAP/SMTP connections.
Stand up secured test mail servers and add integration tests verifying IMAPS/SMTPS connectivity and mail send/receive through the sink.
Document the java-mail-properties attribute and provide a working TLS configuration example.
Add partitionResultsTimeout as a metadata attribute for jobs using the singlestep-partitioning strategy and apply it to the 3 out-of-the-box job definitions.
Update the wiki metadata tables and add/execute verification that the attribute is visible and effective for all importing jobs.
Update the build to Spring Boot 1.2.0.RELEASE and set the ~35 associated dependency versions (Spring 4.1.3, Batch 3.0.2, Security 3.2.5, Jackson 2.4.4, etc.) in the centralized version properties.
Fix compilation errors, deprecated/removed API usages, and behavior changes introduced by the upgraded dependencies across XD modules.
Run the full XD test suite against the upgraded stack, triage failures, and fix regressions caused by the dependency upgrades.
Verify the upgraded runtime in supported deployment modes (single-node, distributed, embedded containers such as Tomcat 8 / Jetty 9.2 / Undertow).
Design and implement support for a separate YAML file carrying deployment manifest properties, including parsing, validation, and merge semantics with inline stream deployment properties.
Unit and integration tests for YML loading, property merging/precedence, and error handling for malformed files.
Document the deployment manifest file format, usage (CLI/REST), and precedence rules.
Design and implement gzip and zip compression/decompression support as a message-bus codec, configurable per stream, integrated with the bus payload conversion pipeline.
Unit and integration tests covering gzip/zip round-trips, interoperability of compressed messages across producers/consumers, and throughput sanity checks.
Document bus compression properties, supported codecs, and performance guidance.
Add compression options to the Rabbit source and sink modules, reusing the U7 codec implementation (compress on sink, decompress on source).
Integration tests deploying Rabbit source/sink streams with compression enabled, verifying end-to-end message integrity for gzip and zip.
Update Rabbit source and sink module documentation with the new compression options.
Integrate all stories on a single branch, resolve cross-story conflicts (notably U5 upgrade vs. new features), and run end-to-end smoke scenarios.
